plain: In 2004, off the coast of San Diego, a Navy fighter pilot named Commander David Fravor says he saw a white oval object shaped like a Tic Tac mint. Michels often repeats Fravor's sense that the thing seemed aware of him, "conscious and almost breathing". Fravor was flying from the aircraft carrier USS Nimitz, and he describes it himself: it was "moving very abruptly over the water like a ping pong ball", then "rapidly accelerated in front of us and disappeared". Michels adds more details across many episodes: it hovered just above the water and seemed to go in and out of it, it climbed to 80,000 feet, and it was already waiting at the meeting point the pilots were heading to next. Other tellers bring in more crew and instruments. A guest named Merrick von Renenamp, retelling the crews' accounts, names other airmen and officers, including Alex Dietrich, Chad Underwood and Kevin Day. Michels mentions radar on the ship USS Princeton. Eric Haseltine, a former official at the National Security Agency (the US eavesdropping agency), says there were too many "independent parallel sensors" on it, and too many people "who didn't want to see it but saw it anyhow". The UFO researcher Jacques Vallee asks why such an object would let "11 f-18s" (Navy fighter jets) chase it "all over the Pacific". Michels notes that the case became widely known through a 2017 New York Times article by the journalist Leslie Kean. If true, it would be a craft far beyond known technology that seemed to notice who was watching it.
